slice: A26 live RTMP — ingest, watch, moderation, replay
verdict: FAIL (moved off BLOCKED; the ingest-plane selection is ruled and the lab has run)

lab.core: two processes from the working tree (VIDRA_ROLE=api on 127.0.0.1:8088 and VIDRA_ROLE=worker), native postgres 16 at schema 136, native redis, STORAGE_BACKEND=local
lab.origin: one origin on 127.0.0.1:8099 — a pipe-only proxy that drops the client's Accept-Encoding, routing /api/* to core and everything else to a production Next standalone server on :3100
lab.ingest: the bundled `media`-profile service: alfg/nginx-rtmp:latest (nginx 1.23.1 + Arut's nginx-rtmp-module, linux/amd64 under emulation) in Docker, running the SHIPPED deploy/media/nginx.conf.template with exactly two lines changed — the shim's api upstream, from api:8080 to host.docker.internal:8090 (a transparent logging proxy in front of core, used to capture the hook contract verbatim)
lab.publisher: ffmpeg 8.1, `-re -f lavfi -i testsrc2 -f lavfi -i sine -c:v libx264 -c:a aac -f flv rtmp://127.0.0.1:1935/live/<key>`, 1280x720@30 + 48 kHz mono AAC; testsrc2 burns a millisecond timecode and a frame counter into the frame, which is what the latency number is read from
lab.rate_limiting: off (RATE_LIMIT_ENABLED=false), so the zero 429s is not a limits observation
not_run: OBS or any real streaming client (ffmpeg was the publisher)
the compose `media` profile itself (docker compose --profile media) — the service definition was rendered and its command reproduced by hand
a second concurrent viewer, and the simultaneous-live caps (live_max_instance_lives / live_max_user_lives)
TLS, a real hostname, or an ingest reachable from another machine
S3 storage: the replay VOD landed on local storage

hook_contract.transport: POST application/x-www-form-urlencoded from nginx-rtmp to a shim on :8082 inside the ingest container, which injects the shared secret header and proxies to the api
hook_contract.auth: X-Ingest-Secret, constant-time compared; the routes 404 when LIVE_INGEST_SECRET is unset

start.name: the RAW STREAM KEY, always
start.refused: 404 for an unknown key, 403 for a policy refusal

stop.name_before_this_slice: the RAW STREAM KEY (the module caches the pre-rename name)
stop.name_after_this_slice: the STREAM ID (the hook now sits on the `hls` application, whose session is named by the id)

wrong_key_publish.hook_message: no live stream for that key
wrong_key_publish.ingest_behaviour: connection dropped ~100 ms after connect; ffmpeg exits 251 'Input/output error'

rotation_while_live.current_publisher: ALLOWED TO FINISH — not disconnected, segments kept being written, state stayed live

sc1_authorization_and_key.rotation_defect_before_the_fix: the stop hook carried the pre-rename raw key, so after a rotation it no longer resolved: 404, the stream stayed `live` for 20+ minutes with no replay, until the duration watchdog closed it

playlist.type: live media playlist served at master.m3u8

ladder.note: the live 'ladder' is exactly whatever the publisher pushes; there is no ABR and no variant playlist

latency_glass_to_glass_s.method: burned-in testsrc2 timecode read from a canvas grab of the decoded frame, against the encoder's own source-time-to-wall-clock anchor (anchor spread 0.13 s)

drift.media_clock_rate: ~0.64x while the buffer grew from 14 s to 60 s
drift.cause: CPU starvation in this lab (a software-rendered headless Chromium beside an x86-emulated ingest and a native x264 encoder); playbackRate stayed 1 and nothing resynced to the live edge

sc3_moderation.admin_terminate_control: DOES NOT EXIST — there is no /admin/live* route in core and no control in the admin UI; an admin gets 404 on DELETE /live/{id} and PATCH /live/{id} because those are owner-scoped

max_duration.publisher: NOT disconnected — the ingest socket lingered and segments kept being written

audit.resource_id: empty — the id is only in free text

sc4_disconnect_and_replay.mechanism: nginx-rtmp records each session to <LIVE_HLS_ROOT>/rec/<stream-id>-<unixtime>.flv; on the stop hook the api opens the newest recording for the stream and pushes it through the ordinary video pipeline (draft, attach original, process)
sc4_disconnect_and_replay.before_the_fix: no recording was EVER written — nginx-rtmp does not create a missing record_path, and the HLS cleanup rmdir()s an empty `rec` (it sits inside hls_path) ~12 s after start; every session logged 'live replay: no recording for finished session'
sc4_disconnect_and_replay.grace_window: none — the state flips on the stop hook; re-publishing with the same key restarts the SAME stream row as a NEW session with a new started_at, and an `ended` one-shot stream is fully reusable

valid_secret_no_rtmp_publish.watch_page: no <video> element at all; 'Can't play this live stream / Your browser could not play the live video feed.' beside a LIVE badge

sc6_capability_truth.studio_with_live_unavailable: the Live-streams header is down to Reload, no create control anywhere on the page; existing streams stay listed and manageable
sc6_capability_truth.admin_system_live_component: NONE — ten components (clamav, ffmpeg, mfa_kek, postgres, redis, s3, search, settings_sync, smtp, storage) and not one of them watches the ingest, so a dead RTMP plane leaves /admin/system reading ok

admin_infrastructure.note: static config echo, not a probe

defects_fixed: the on-publish redirect answered an rtmp:// Location, which nginx-rtmp reads as a PUSH RELAY target rather than a rename, so HLS was written under the raw stream key and the api 404d the whole broadcast
the HLS module never sees a rename (reverse module order), so packaging moved to a second loopback-only `hls` application fed by a push
the recorder directory was never created and, when empty, was deleted by the HLS cleanup — no session had ever been recorded and replay had never run
a mid-broadcast key rotation orphaned the session (stop hook 404, stream stuck live) — the stop hook moved to the `hls` application, whose session is named by the id
the public stream ID was accepted as a publish identity, making the stream key decorative
a deactivated owner could still publish and be listed on the public rail
findings_open: no admin control terminates a live stream
the duration watchdog is server-side only: the publisher keeps ingesting and keeps writing segments and a recording
live audit rows leave resource_id empty and carry the stream id only in free-text reason
session recordings are never deleted after the replay publishes (six .flv files, 66 MB, still on the volume at the end of the lab)
a hook-only flip puts a stream with no bytes on the public Live-now rail
no live ABR ladder and no viewer count
nothing resyncs a drifted live player to the edge
the ingest image is pinned to alfg/nginx-rtmp:latest, a 2022 build
